name: Carca
tagline: Sun-baked stone, banners, a walled town
lineage: New — not yet defined anywhere but here.
story: DRAFT — a sketch to rewrite in your own words. The guess, from the name (Carcassonne?): a walled hill town in the south. Warm limestone, moss in the joints, painted banners against the stone, everything built to last and carved rather than printed. Headings read like inscriptions; the accent is a banner red-orange you can see from outside the walls.
principles: Stone first: warm greys and limestone carry everything, colour arrives as a banner.
Carved, not drawn — type is inscriptional, edges are chamfered, nothing is flimsy.
Built to last: heavy borders, honest weight, no translucency.
Heraldry for meaning — a small set of banner colours, each standing for something.
do: Set headings in caps with wide tracking, like an inscription.
Use thick borders and small radii — chamfers, not curves.
Hang the banner colours sparingly against the stone.
dont: No glass, no gloss, no blur.
No pastels — every colour must survive weather.
No thin hairlines; nothing here is fragile.

voice.tone: Declarative and brief, like words that had to be carved.

motion.character: Solid. Things land with weight and stay put; nothing floats.

texture.notes: Coursed stone — a joint line every course, blocks flat and barely darker at the bed. A true running bond would stagger the head joints; that needs a tile cut both ways, so it isn't drawn. Hard drop shadows — offset, no blur — like noon light on a wall.

notes: DRAFT seeded as a starting point — every value here is a guess for the editor to correct, especially the story.
